explanation: The indicial roots are 3/2 and 1/2, differing by 1. The standard second-solution form is b₋₁y₁(x)ln(x)+x^(1/2)Σbₙxⁿ, matching option b when y₁ is the actual first solution. However, the stated first solution x²Σaₙxⁿ is inconsistent with these roots; it should begin with x^(3/2). Thus b matches the corrected problem, but the literal stated general solution is invalid. Frobenius theory for ordinary differential equations is absent from the supplied course topics, so this is prerequisite.
